You have reached the end of the guided course. Completion here means that you can explain the workflow and carry it out on the provided practice files; it does **not** certify a production analysis or replace project-specific review.

## Readiness checklist

Use this checklist before applying the workflow to a study:

- [ ] I can explain what raw acceleration captures—and what it does not directly measure.
- [ ] I can document device ID, participant ID, placement, orientation, dates, time zone, and wear protocol.
- [ ] I can preserve raw files and create a traceable download and conversion log.
- [ ] I can distinguish calibration, non-wear, clipping, file completeness, and valid-day decisions.
- [ ] I can record the GGIR version and all analysis parameters used.
- [ ] I can review daily and nightly outputs without treating automated classifications as ground truth.
- [ ] I can merge participant-level results while checking ID uniqueness and merge coverage.
- [ ] I can describe the limitations of cut-points, sleep windows, missingness, and measurement error.
- [ ] I can reproduce an exclusion from an explicit rule and audit log.

## Finish the practice pathway

1. [Take or retry the final knowledge check](knowledge-checking.qmd).
2. [Download the course toolkit](toolkit.qmd).
3. Complete the capstone with the synthetic files.
4. Compare your output with the included answer key and expected dataset.
5. Adapt the checklist and data dictionary to your own protocol before production use.

::: {.callout-important}
## A defensible result is more than a successful script

Keep the original raw data, the software version, the full configuration, a processing log, quality-review decisions, and the final data dictionary together. Those records are what allow a result to be checked and reproduced.
:::

## Continue learning

- Review the [glossary](glossary.qmd) and [references](references.qmd).
- Check the [current GGIR documentation](https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/).
- Send a correction or accessibility report through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/eryx-lee/accelerometer-learning-course/issues).

Your progress is stored only in this browser. You can revisit any module without losing access to the material.
